diagnosis:
The model was calibrated on all of 1971-1997 (after a one-year warm-up) for NSE. I ran a global DDS search (3000 runs) and then refined it with Nelder-Mead (600 runs). Calibration fit is high: NSE 0.934, KGE 0.92, r 0.967. Simulated flow is about 4.5% too high on average (PBIAS +4.5%), so the model slightly over-predicts water volume, probably in summer when it underestimates evaporation.

The final parameters: FC about 340 mm, LP 0.94 and BETA 7.6 (a large, nonlinear soil store); fast response (K0 0.30, K1 0.29, UZL 13 mm, MAXBAS 2.3 days); K2 0.14, so baseflow also drains quickly. This fits a flashy catchment on low-productivity fractured rock in a wet climate. Snow hardly matters here (about 0.6% of precipitation), so the snow parameters are poorly constrained but have little effect.

Weak points: peak flows from the largest storms are slightly too low (simulated maximum 23.7 vs 28.1 mm/day observed), and summer recessions and low flows are likely less accurate. I did not test the parameters on a held-out period, so I can't show how well they transfer. FC and BETA trade off against each other: DDS found a different combination (FC 242, BETA 5.0) with almost the same NSE (0.932). I'm fairly confident about the response parameters and less so about the soil parameters. I expect the independent-period NSE to be around 0.88-0.92.
